summary: At 13:51:00Z config change cfg-0139 cut fivo-api's DB_POOL_SIZE from 10 to 2 (dashboard, dev). The engine has max_overflow=0 and pool_timeout=5.0 s, so requests that cannot get one of 2 connections wait 5 s and fail with sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError. The first such error is at 13:52:03Z, db_connections is a flat 2 from 13:52Z, and p95 is pinned at 5006 ms. The 5xx errors are partial and span many DB routes, while /health stays 200. Restoring DB_POOL_SIZE to 10 is the immediate mitigation. This has not yet been confirmed by reverting.

root_cause.component: DB_POOL_SIZE env var (cfg-0139), SQLAlchemy engine in app/db.py
root_cause.summary: cfg-0139 reduced DB_POOL_SIZE from 10 to 2 at 13:51:00Z. With max_overflow=0 and a 5 s pool timeout, concurrent requests that each hold a session exhaust the 2-connection pool and fail with QueuePool timeouts. This produces 500s and the 5006 ms latency ceiling on every DB-backed route.

hypotheses.statement: Config change cfg-0139 (DB_POOL_SIZE 10 -> 2 at 13:51Z) starved fivo-api's connection pool, so DB-backed requests hit the 5 s pool timeout and return 500.

supporting.statement: All 28 error lines in 13:48-14:00Z are 'QueuePool limit of size 2 overflow 0 reached ... timeout 5.00'. The first is at 13:52:03Z, after the change.
db_connections is a flat 2.0 from 13:52Z. error_rate was 0.0 through 13:50Z and rose from 13:51Z to 0.6071 by 13:59Z.
Code sets pool_size from DB_POOL_SIZE, max_overflow=0 and pool_timeout=5.0. This matches the 5006 ms p95 ceiling.
Errors span many routes while /health stays 200. Successful requests continue, which fits partial pool starvation.

contradicting.statement: error_rate 0.0333 at 13:51Z precedes the first error log by about a minute. This is unexplained but small. The 5-minute metrics show onset in the 13:50 bucket, which is bucket granularity.

hypotheses.statement: Deploy dep-0414 (b139bb3, 'access log: record the request id') introduced a regression causing 500s and stalls.

supporting.statement: It was deployed 9 minutes before the 13:50 onset on code that runs on every request.

contradicting.statement: The diff only adds one request_id key to the access log, plus README lines. It has no I/O, DB or session code.
The first error is at 13:52:03Z, and errors are pool timeouts naming size 2.

hypotheses.statement: neon-postgres is slow, suspended or at its connection limit, as in INC-2026-024.

supporting.statement: A past incident had QueuePool timeouts caused by a Neon cold start. This is a lead only.

contradicting.statement: No Neon deploys or config changes were found.
Neon logs show only routine checkpoint lines.
slow_queries was 0 throughout. Active connections fell at 13:50Z instead of saturating.
The errors are client-side pool timeouts of size 2.

hypotheses.statement: The single 512 MB fivo-api instance is out of memory or CPU, or thrashing.

supporting.statement: fivo-api runs on one 512 MB instance shared by all routes.

contradicting.statement: Memory stayed at 198.7-208.0 MB and CPU at 6.6-22.5% with no shift.
Only two restarts occurred, at 13:41Z and 13:51Z, each matching a change. None followed.

facts.statement: cfg-0139 at 13:51:00Z changed fivo-api DB_POOL_SIZE from 10 to 2, by dashboard:dev, with the note 'stay under the database plan's connection limit'.
Deploy dep-0414 (b139bb3) went live at 13:41:00Z. Its diff only adds a request_id key to the access log, plus README lines.
All 28 error lines in 13:48-14:00Z are QueuePool size 2 timeout errors. The first is at 13:52:03Z.
db_connections is a constant 2.0 from 13:52Z to 14:24Z. Before that it ranged 2-8.
error_rate was 0.0 from 13:45Z to 13:50Z and reached 0.6071 by 13:59Z.
p95 latency sat at 5006 ms from 13:55Z to 14:20Z. Baseline mean was about 932 ms.
500s span /transactions, /summary, quick-add, /receipts and /categories. The health check returned 200 throughout.
The engine uses pool_size=settings.db_pool_size, max_overflow=0 and pool_timeout=5.0 s. Sessions are request-scoped.
Neon had no deploys or config changes and slow_queries was 0. fivo-api memory and CPU were flat.

assumptions: The 13:51Z restart is probably the instance restarting to apply the env var. This is inferred from timing.
Sessions may stay open during the quick-add worker wait and the insights LLM call. This is inferred, not proven, and does not change the conclusion.
No evidence quantifies concurrent connection hold times. Saturation of a pool of 2 at the observed request rate is inferred.
The 13:50 onset in the 5-minute metrics is assumed to be bucket granularity, because 1-minute data shows errors starting after 13:51Z.

recommended_actions.action: Restore fivo-api DB_POOL_SIZE to 10 (revert cfg-0139) and watch error_rate, p95 and db_connections.
recommended_actions.rationale: This restores the pre-change pool cap, under which there were no errors. It also confirms the cause.

recommended_actions.action: If the database plan's connection limit is a real concern, pick a pool size from measured concurrent use (db_connections reached 8 before the change). Shorten session lifetime in quick-add and insights so they do not hold a session across the worker wait or the LLM call.
recommended_actions.rationale: The change was meant to stay under a plan limit, but 2 is too small for the demand. Long-held sessions make a small pool saturate.

recommended_actions.action: Alert on QueuePool TimeoutError counts and on db_connections pinned at the pool cap. Add review or a staged rollout for pool-size env var changes. Add a health check that touches the DB.
recommended_actions.rationale: /health stayed 200 while many routes failed for over 30 minutes, and detection came about 15 minutes after onset.

missing_evidence: No revert of DB_POOL_SIZE has been tried yet, so recovery is unconfirmed.
There is no separate pool checked-out metric, so in-use connections cannot be told apart from the cap.
Error lines 0017-0028 were seen only as summaries. Their route and duration fields were not read.
The single fivo-worker warning line (logagg:fivo-worker:0001) was never read.
Neon's external status page could not be checked.

what_changed.what_changed: DB_POOL_SIZE was reduced from 10 to 2 on fivo-api via the dashboard (cfg-0139). Pre-change demand reached 8 connections, so a cap of 2 is too small.

before.statement: Pool cap was 10. db_connections ranged 2-8 (mean about 5.1) and error_rate was 0.0 every minute from 13:45Z to 13:50Z. There were no QueuePool errors before 13:52:03Z.

after.statement: Pool cap is 2. db_connections is a constant 2.0 from 13:52Z to 14:24Z. QueuePool 'size 2 overflow 0 ... timeout 5.00' errors start at 13:52:03Z, and error_rate reaches 0.2143 at 13:52Z and 0.6071 by 13:59Z.

changes_considered.change: deploy on fivo-api: commit b139bb3 "access log: record the request id" by github-actions
changes_considered.reason: The diff only adds a request_id key to the access log and 2 README lines, with no I/O, DB or session code. No errors appeared between the 13:41Z deploy and 13:52:03Z. All errors are pool timeouts that name the new pool size of 2.

changes_considered.change: config on fivo-api: DB_POOL_SIZE: 10 -> 2 by dashboard:dev ("stay under the database plan's connection limit")
changes_considered.reason: DB_POOL_SIZE was cut from 10 to 2 at 13:51:00Z. The first QueuePool 'size 2' error is at 13:52:03Z, db_connections is a flat 2 from 13:52Z, and errors are 5006 ms pool timeouts on every DB route. Before the change there were no errors, with demand up to 8 connections.
